brief: Find an identifier through the current 256-byte record, always checking the base.
decl: std::uint32_t record_stack_contains(std::span<const std::byte> records, std::uint32_t base, std::uint32_t cursor, std::uint32_t identifier);
notes: Original bytes and execution establish argument widths and access order.
Spans are host byte views; original 32-bit address identities are explicit where needed.

bookkeeping.scope: Complete original body on supplied scalar state and valid byte spans. Copy cases include overlapping and unaligned views with the original read/write order.
bookkeeping.supported_domain: Readable identifier words in a supplied nonwrapping address window. The base record is always examined, including a null cursor. No original fault or wrapped-address traversal claim.
bookkeeping.acceptance: Met: 200 synthetic original-execution cases matched bit-exact by MSVC and Zig/Clang runners. See docs/recovery/record-stack.md.
